questions.q: What are the three primary components that make up a single DNA nucleotide?
options: A deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base
A ribose sugar, a sulfate group, and a pyrimidine base
An amino acid, a peptide bond, and a lipid
A pair of homologous chromosomes and a mitochondrial envelope
questions.explain: According to the fundamental principles of DNA structure, a single nucleotide consists of a deoxyribose sugar molecule, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base. Source: DNA Structure: Nucleotides.

questions.q: In a double-stranded DNA molecule, which of the following represents the correct complementary base pairing rules?
options: Adenine pairs with Cytosine; Guanine pairs with Thymine
Adenine pairs with Guanine; Cytosine pairs with Thymine
Adenine pairs with Thymine; Cytosine pairs with Guanine
Adenine pairs with Uracil; Guanine pairs with Cytosine
questions.explain: Chargaff's rules state that in DNA, Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T), and Cytosine (C) always pairs with Guanine (G). Source: DNA Structure: base pairing (A-T, C-G).

questions.q: If a forensic scientist discovers a DNA sequence that reads 5'-A-T-G-C-C-A-3', what would the complementary strand's sequence be?
questions.explain: Following complementary base pairing rules, A pairs with T and C pairs with G. Thus, A-T-G-C-C-A pairs with T-A-C-G-G-T. Source: DNA Structure: base pairing.

questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are found in the nucleus of a normal human somatic cell?
questions.explain: Human somatic cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes, totaling 46 chromosomes. These contain the nuclear DNA inherited from both parents. Source: DNA Structure: chromosomes.

questions.q: Which chemical structure makes up the 'backbone' or outer side-rails of the DNA double helix?
options: Paired nitrogenous bases linked by hydrogen bonds
Alternating deoxyribose sugar molecules and phosphate groups
Polypeptide chains of amino acids
Strands of RNA interwoven with lipids
questions.explain: The DNA backbone consists of alternating deoxyribose sugar and phosphate groups, connected by phosphodiester bonds. The rungs of the ladder are the nitrogenous bases. Source: DNA Structure.

questions.q: The stability of the DNA double helix relies on chemical bonds between the nitrogenous bases of opposite strands. What type of bond connects Adenine to Thymine and Cytosine to Guanine?
options: Covalent bonds
Hydrogen bonds
Ionic bonds
Metallic bonds
questions.explain: Weak hydrogen bonds link the complementary nitrogenous base pairs (2 bonds between A-T, 3 bonds between C-G). These are easily broken by heat during the denaturation step of PCR.
